title: Logins and hospital set-up
intro: How people get into Vaidyx-TB and how a hospital is set up the first time. Today every account is a plain Vaidyx login typed in by an admin, and a forgotten password needs the Vaidyx admin.

questions.question: How should a new doctor get a Vaidyx-TB account?

options.label: Admin invites, doctor completes (Recommended)
options.description: The department admin enters name, mobile and role; the doctor opens a one-time invite, sets a password and fills the profile.

options.label: Admin creates it fully (today)
options.description: The admin types the login name and password and hands them over; the doctor fills nothing.

options.label: Self sign-up, admin approves
options.description: Doctors register and pick their department; nothing opens until the department admin approves.

questions.why: Today the department admin creates plain Vaidyx logins (login, password, display name, Doctor or Head) and hands the credentials over (S5, J5, tumour_board/accounts.py). The main app has an open sign-up switch, off by default. UX note 4 (IKEA effect: people value what they build themselves). Shapes T20 (admin screens).

questions.question: Who should create the logins of residents, PGs and fellows?

options.label: Department admin, like doctors (Recommended)
options.description: All logins of a department stay in one list; the admin marks the person Resident, PG or fellow.

options.label: Their consultant invites them
options.description: Faster when a new PG batch arrives; the department admin can still see and disable them.

options.label: Self sign-up, consultant approves
options.description: Residents register, name their consultant, and wait for that consultant's approval.

questions.why: Settled: residents are registered in their department and join Case Files with a code (notes role-treating, role-resident; I03). Today they use the consultant's login, so the audit shows only the consultant (G14, S5). R02 (role list) defines the role; R06 builds the team on top.

questions.question: Should resident, PG and fellow logins carry an end date?

options.label: Yes, course or posting end (Recommended)
options.description: Access stops by itself on that date (for example the end of a 3-year MD or MS); the admin can extend it.

options.label: No end date
options.description: Logins stay until an admin disables them; leavers depend on someone remembering.

options.label: End date for visiting fellows only
options.description: Short-term fellows and observers expire; the hospital's own PGs do not.

questions.why: Disabling is manual and global today (G17, J5). Trainees leave on known dates, unlike consultants. R03 (access ending when someone leaves a team) decides what happens to their Case File access.

questions.question: How should people sign in?

options.label: Password; SMS OTP when available (Recommended)
options.description: Works today on the hospital network with no outside service; phone OTP is switched on once the hospital has an SMS gateway.

options.label: Mobile number and SMS OTP
options.description: No password to forget; needs a DLT-registered SMS gateway (a monthly cost) and phone signal at every sign-in.

options.label: Password and OTP every time
options.description: Strongest; adds an SMS wait to every sign-in, also on the OPD desktop.

options.label: Email OTP
options.description: Needs the server to send mail, which Vaidyx does not do today.

questions.why: Today: password (8 characters minimum), sessions of 7 days; the main app also has optional authenticator-app codes (core/auth.py, TOTP). Phone OTP is common in Indian apps; commercial SMS in India needs TRAI DLT registration. Vaidyx sends no email or SMS (changes_v2 section 3, in-app first).

questions.question: What should people type as their login name?

options.label: Mobile number (Recommended)
options.description: Easy to remember; the same number fills the phone call button and any later SMS OTP.

options.label: A login name (today)
options.description: For example dr.meena.rad, chosen by the admin; people forget the spelling.

options.label: Hospital employee ID
options.description: Matches the hospital's staff records; new residents and visiting fellows may not have one yet.

questions.why: Login names today are 2 to 63 lower-case letters, digits, dots or hyphens (accounts.py). Settled: on phones a call option opens the dialer with the person's number (R11), so the mobile number is needed anyway.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R04-Q04 answered 'Mobile number and SMS OTP' (the mobile number is then the login).

questions.question: Which accounts should need a second step at sign-in?

options.label: Admins only (Recommended)
options.description: Root, department and Vaidyx admins also enter a code from an authenticator app (already in Vaidyx); doctors sign in with one step.

options.label: Admins and MDT Coordinators
options.description: Coordinators open every Case File, so they get the second step too.

options.label: Everyone
options.description: Every sign-in takes one more step, also for busy treating and supporting doctors.

options.label: No one
options.description: Fastest; a leaked password opens the account.

questions.why: The Vaidyx admin holds a server shell tool and sees everything (role-vaidyxadmin); the coordinator may open every Case File (matrix read_case). Passwords were exposed before (K06). Authenticator codes already exist in core/auth.py.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R04-Q04 answered 'Password and OTP every time' (everyone already has a second step).

questions.question: Who should reset a forgotten password?

options.label: Department admin, one-time password (Recommended)
options.description: The admin issues a one-time password; the doctor must set a new one at the next sign-in; audited. Needs a small change to the Vaidyx login system.

options.label: Self-service by SMS OTP
options.description: No admin needed; works only once the hospital has an SMS gateway.

options.label: Vaidyx admin only (today)
options.description: One person for the whole hospital; doctors wait until they are reached.

questions.why: Today a reset needs the Vaidyx admin: the login system changes a password only with the current one (accounts.py RESET_NOTE; J5 friction; role-deptadmin 'Reset a password' under cannot). The V2 plan (section 4, item 2.3) meant department admins to reset.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R04-Q04 answered 'Mobile number and SMS OTP' (there are no passwords).

questions.question: When should Vaidyx sign people out on its own?

options.label: 30 min idle on shared PCs (Recommended)
options.description: The sign-in screen asks 'shared computer?'; shared OPD computers sign out after 30 idle minutes; a personal phone stays signed in up to 7 days.

options.label: Keep 7 days everywhere (today)
options.description: Fewer sign-ins; a shared computer stays open for the next person.

options.label: When the browser closes
options.description: Safest on shared computers; a sign-in every time.

questions.why: Sessions last 7 days today (core/auth.py TOKEN_TTL). Treating doctors work on OPD desktops and phones (role-treating devices). R15 (patient data on phones) builds on this.

questions.question: Which details should each person's profile hold?

options.label: Name, designation and photo (Recommended)
options.description: Shown on Case Files, team lists and the board room, so people see who did what.

options.label: Mobile number
options.description: Fills the call button and any SMS codes; seen only by colleagues.

options.label: Medical registration number
options.description: The State Medical Council or NMC number, shown beside the name; never used to sign.

options.label: Qualification and unit
options.description: For example MD, MS, DNB, DM or MCh, and the consultant's unit; helps link residents to their unit.

questions.why: Today only a display name is stored (org.py users). UX note 4 (IKEA effect): ask more than email and password. The mobile number serves the settled phone call option (R11).

questions.question: How long should the set-up at the first sign-in be?

options.label: Three short steps, skippable (Recommended)
options.description: Profile and photo, then a theme, with a progress bar that does not start at 0; about one minute; anything skipped can be done later.

options.label: Only set a new password
options.description: Straight to work; the profile stays bare.

options.label: Full profile before any use
options.description: Nothing opens until every profile field is filled.

questions.why: UX note 4 (IKEA effect: name, theme, design) and note 5 (progress bar not from 0). The theme choices themselves and any tour style are R18; this sets only how much the first sign-in asks.

questions.question: What should a doctor see right after the first sign-in?

options.label: A ready sample Case File (Recommended)
options.description: A SYNTHETIC patient, already fetched and checked, shows what Vaidyx does before the doctor does any work; kept apart from real Case Files and hidden with one tap.

options.label: Their own work list
options.description: My Case Files and the inbox, empty at first, with one Create button.

options.label: A short guided tour
options.description: Tips point at the parts of the real home, one by one.

options.label: Check one patient now
options.description: Type one UHID and see the records fetched and what is missing in seconds; the profile comes after.

questions.why: UX note 3 (gift first, like Duolingo). Today the home shows '3 steps to start' and one section per role (home.py, UI_PLAN_OCT15). Demo and real Case Files are mixed today (U18), so a sample must stay clearly separate (R15). Merged with R18 'gift first' in validation (17 Oct).

questions.question: What must the root admin finish before doctors can start?

options.label: Name, NCG level, PM-JAY only (Recommended)
options.description: As today; the rest starts from defaults (12-month fetch window, four board heads, placeholder emails) and is changed later.

options.label: Also a working HIS test
options.description: No Case File can be created until a test lookup in the hospital system succeeds.

options.label: Every set-up step
options.description: Departments, emails, department admins, the coordinator and board heads are all done before any doctor signs in.

questions.why: The first set-up today asks hospital name, NCG level (Essential or Optimal: decides which records are required) and PM-JAY empanelled, answered once (S2, home.py); the live app never answered it (K07). T20 kept: set-up as a short guided flow. UX note 1 (sensible defaults).

questions.question: Which contact should each department have in the set-up?

options.label: Email and desk phone (Recommended)
options.description: Request mail drafts and a call button both reach the department's reporting desk.

options.label: Email only (today)
options.description: Placeholder addresses until the hospital gives real ones; no call button for departments.

options.label: A named person with mobile
options.description: Requests and calls go to one person per department, who must be kept current.

questions.why: Department emails are placeholders today (id@hospital.example; S3, changes_v2 section 11). Settled: a call option on phones. How requests travel (in-app, mail, phone, WhatsApp) is R08; notification channels are R14.

questions.question: Besides creating logins, what else may a department admin do?

options.label: Edit department contacts (Recommended)
options.description: Email and desk phone change without asking the root admin.

options.label: See last sign-in per login
options.description: Spots unused or shared logins in the department.

options.label: Mark a doctor on leave
options.description: That doctor's Case File alerts go to a named colleague until they return.

questions.why: Department admins create, disable and remove doctor logins and have no clinical access (role-deptadmin, matrix manage_department, G05). Password reset is R04-Q07; the residents' list is R06.
